andrew_sales: Quick check — ACME needs private connectivity for the POC. They want PrivateLink to our hosted control plane and an interface endpoint for inference APIs. What exact subnet/route/security guidance should we give? Also they'll need temporary API keys and rotation plan.

acme_poc_admin: Prefer PrivateLink (no peering). Security team only allows interface endpoints and a small set of IP ranges. We can provide subnets in two AZs.

sara_se: OK — steps: 1) Create Interface VPCE for service name `com.redwood-inference.us-west-2.vpce` (we'll provide service name). 2) Pick two private subnets (one per AZ) for ENIs. 3) Attach security group allowing outbound TLS to our endpoint and inbound from the ENIs if needed. 4) Private DNS: enable so `api.redwood.ai` resolves to the VPCE. 5) No route table changes required for the interface endpoint itself.

jon_net: To expand — interface endpoints create ENIs in your subnets. No explicit route entries. If they instead choose VPC peering, add routes for our service CIDR(s) to the peering connection. For peering you'd need both route table and security updates. Our recommendation: PrivateLink for cross-account POCs.

acme_poc_admin: What's the minimal SG rule we should add? We have tight egress rules.

sara_se: Minimal: allow outbound TCP 443 to the VPCE's service IPs (or just allow outbound to 0.0.0.0/0 if you already permit that for outbound TLS). Inbound isn't required for requests initiated from your VPC to our API. Example SG egress rule:

```
Type: HTTPS
Protocol: TCP
Port: 443
Destination: vpce-xxxx-service-ip-ranges OR 0.0.0.0/0
```

If you enforce destination IPs, we can provide the announced VPCE addresses once the endpoint is created (they're ENIs in your account).

sam_security: A couple security notes: 1) Turn on private DNS for the endpoint (so the normal hostnames resolve internally). 2) Audit that the endpoint's policy is restricted to the account IDs (we can provide the account numbers to allow). 3) API key rotation: we'll issue a time-limited key (30d) for the POC and require rotation via HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager — whichever the customer prefers.

andrew_sales: Customer asks about Private Hosted Zone association — will that collide with their existing private zone for `redwood.ai`? They want to retain their internal DNS.

jon_net: Private DNS for an interface endpoint will create AZ-specific DNS entries for the service name in your VPC; it shouldn't overwrite unrelated hosted zones. If you have a private hosted zone for `redwood.ai` already, we recommend using a subdomain or coordinate DNS records with your DNS team. Alternatively we can provide a CNAME to the VPCE hostname.

acme_poc_admin: They also want to lock IP egress to our service only. Can we provide a simple list of service IPs pre-provision? Preferably not dynamic.

sara_se: We can't pre-publish static global IPs for hosted endpoints — interface ENIs are allocated from your subnets. For stricter egress allowlisting you can: 1) Create the VPCE first, then inspect the ENI IPs (stable while endpoint exists) and lock them in your ACLs. 2) Or use a NAT with stateful inspection and restrict on DNS/FQDN — but that's brittle. For enterprise POCs some customers request Dedicated pools which allow IP-based controls via peered networks or static egress IPs; we can scope that in a follow-up.

sam_security: If they need strict non-changing egress IPs, propose Dedicated with transit/VPN or a static egress appliance. We'll flag as 'enterprise requirement'.

andrew_sales: Noted. Action items: (A) Sara to share exact service name and account IDs for endpoint policy. (B) Jon to write minimal SG + route checklist (one-liner) for the customer. (C) Sam to propose API key rotation + vault approach. (D) I'll schedule 30-min handoff call with ACME network on Wed.

deploy-bot: Created ticket INF-4932 for 'ACME POC PrivateLink setup' assigned to sara_se and jon_net.

sara_se: I'll DM the service name and account numbers. Sample CLI we usually paste for customers:

```
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \
  --vpc-id vpc-0abc1234 \
  --service-name com.redwood-inference.us-west-2.vpce \
  --vpc-endpoint-type Interface \
  --subnet-ids subnet-aaa subnet-bbb \
  --security-group-ids sg-xxxx
```

jon_net: And sample route table note for peering if they ask:

```
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-xxx --destination-cidr-block 10.12.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-xxx
```

acme_poc_admin: Great — thanks. We'll try to create the endpoint tomorrow and loop back with ENI IPs for allowlist verification.

andrew_sales: Perfect, I'll set the handoff call and send calendar invite. :thumbsup:
